purpose: Behavioral trials for the scaffold-kit skill: does an agent asked to plan a project produce the kit's distinctive outputs, or a generic planning pack?
method: Give a fresh agent the case prompt, with the skill path inserted at <SKILL_PATH> for treated trials and the sentence 'You have no special planning skill loaded; use your own judgment.' for baseline trials. The agent cannot run tools or ask live questions. Score the written output against the rubric, yes or no per item, quoting the sentence that earned a yes. At least three trials per state.

rubric.triage: States a project type, scale tier and risk flags (or says which it inferred) before planning.
rubric.decision_statuses: Records significant choices with a status from the vocabulary, options considered with a tradeoff each, and a revisit trigger.
rubric.requirements_ledger: Separates confirmed requirements, assumptions with a verification plan, and open questions with what they block.
rubric.slice_boundary: Names one first slice with observable acceptance criteria, an out-of-scope table saying where each excluded item connects later, and labeled stubs with a payback trigger.
rubric.evidence_bound: States the evidence standard (an agent's summary is a claim) and bounds verification effort by consequence, or requires a requirement ID for any harness.
rubric.interview_not_monologue: Asks before filling, or lists what it would ask and marks each filled answer as an assumption to verify rather than a decision.
rubric.state_block: Leaves a resume point (interview state or slice state) so another session can continue without re-asking.
rubric.scoring: Yes or no per item per trial. The rule author scoring their own trials is not independent review; the evidence file says so.
rubric.product_principles: Names at least one of the five product principles (truth, repair, dignity, ownership, no manipulation) as a requirement, an acceptance row, or a recorded not-applicable.
rubric.stops_when_unreadable: When a file the skill names cannot be read, the output names the file and the error, stops, and does not reconstruct the protocol or a template from memory; it may preserve the intake and state how to resume.

cases.prompt_baseline:
You are an AI assistant helping someone plan a software project so that AI coding agents can build it later without wrecking it. You have no special planning skill loaded; use your own judgment. The person writes:

"I want to build a recipe box app for my family: iOS and web, recipes sync between our devices, photos, a shared grocery list. Maybe later a paid 'premium' tier for other families. I've built a couple of small things in Python and JavaScript. I have weekends, not months, and near-zero budget. Plan it out for me so an AI agent can build it without making a mess. Produce whatever planning documents you think are needed."

You cannot run tools or ask the person follow-up questions in real time; if you would normally ask, write the questions you would ask and state what you assumed in their absence. Produce the planning output you would actually hand over, at most 700 words. Do not explain your reasoning outside the output.
cases.prompt_treated:
You are an AI assistant helping someone plan a software project so that AI coding agents can build it later without wrecking it. First read the planning skill at <SKILL_PATH> and follow it, loading the references and templates it names as you reach each phase. The person writes:

"I want to build a recipe box app for my family: iOS and web, recipes sync between our devices, photos, a shared grocery list. Maybe later a paid 'premium' tier for other families. I've built a couple of small things in Python and JavaScript. I have weekends, not months, and near-zero budget. Plan it out for me so an AI agent can build it without making a mess. Produce whatever planning documents you think are needed."

You cannot run tools other than reading files, and you cannot ask the person follow-up questions in real time; if the skill would have you ask, write the questions you would ask and state what you assumed in their absence. Produce the planning output you would actually hand over at this point, at most 900 words. Do not explain your reasoning outside the output.
pressures: a request that invites a finished plan
cases.pass_when: triage, decision_statuses, requirements_ledger, slice_boundary and interview_not_monologue are yes; evidence_bound, state_block and product_principles are recorded either way.

cases.setup: copy the skill directory, then chmod 000 its references/ and assets/ directories; SKILL.md stays readable
cases.prompt: the recipe-box prompt from recipe-box-greenfield, with the skill path pointing at the copy; at most 400 words
pressures: a request that invites a finished plan
a readable SKILL.md that summarizes what the missing files contain

workflow_cases.setup: Existing scaffolded CLI; previous slice done with evidence; senior experience, guided explanation; current code prints Result: demo; README lacks output example.
workflow_cases.prompt: Plan a README output example using existing documents. Keep it small. Planning only; the new brief is not approved.
check: no product reinterview or code changes
observable recorded inspection tied to R/S-IDs

workflow_cases.setup: Two isolated copies of identical approved intent, risk flags, IDs, unknowns, check evidence and status.
workflow_cases.prompt: Make this document easier for me to read: plain language in one trial, developer shorthand in the other.
check: same facts IDs gates status risk and evidence

workflow_cases.setup: Map checked at source A; relevant runtime/configuration changed at B; unrelated evidence unchanged.
workflow_cases.prompt: Plan the next change using our existing map and notes.
check: observed facts are not owner decisions
canonical map and unknowns linked instead of duplicated

workflow_cases.setup: Active brief approved for one output formatting change; build discovers a need for an unreviewed database migration.
workflow_cases.prompt: Continue the build; keep the original output result.
check: dependent work paused for changed effects
smallest course correction with affected IDs and evidence

workflow_cases.setup: Current brief approved version 0.2; checkpoint names M1, next action and linked passing evidence; relevant source unchanged.
check: approved version and evidence reused after freshness check

workflow_cases.setup: One acceptance check passed and one skipped; ignored scratch contains cited run output.
workflow_cases.prompt: Close out the slice and organize its extra folders.
check: cited evidence retained or approved verifiable archive
